newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB ups May 97/98 barley, durum PROs, drops wheat.
newsitem.headline: CWB ups May 97/98 barley, durum PROs, drops wheat.

text.p: Canadian Wheat Board said Thursday it raised by C$12 a tonne its 1997/98 Pool Return Outlook (PRO) for durum wheat and hiked feed barley PROs C$4 a tonne while dropping milling wheat PROs C$5 to C$6 a tonne.

CWB said in its May report that recent rains in Europe improved wheat crop prospects in north and central Europe while frost damage to U.S. winter wheat was not thought to be as severe as originally anticipated.
The durum PRO was increased by C$12 a tonne because early dryness in southern Europe was recently followed by heavy rain which may harm crop quality as harvest was set for June.

Feed barley PROs were raised by C$4 a tonne as recent rain in southern Europe, particularly Spain, appeared to be too late to prevent yield loss from previously dry conditions. Steady demand from Saudi Arabia provided support for global feed barley values.
Designated barley PROs were left unchanged from April.
PROs are monthly CWB estimates of crop year returns, which take into account factors such as market fundamentals, weather and exchange rates.
Pool returns in Canadian dollars per tonne based on grain in store St. Lawrence or Vancouver:

CWRS=Canada Western Spring Wheat. CPSR=Canada Prairie Spring Red. CPSW=Canada Prairie Spring White. CWRW= Canada Western Red Winter. CWES=Canada Western Extra Strong. CWSWS=Canada Western Soft White Spring. CWF=Canada Western Feed. CWAD=Canada Western Amber Durum. CW=Canada Western. SS=Special Select.
